newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina announces graft crackdown in customs.
newsitem.headline: Argentina announces graft crackdown in customs.

text.p: The Argentine government announced a crackdown on graft in the customs service on Friday that included the appointment of new administrators and dismissal of staff.
Government tax chief Carlos Silvani said in a statement he named Navy Capt. Antonio Angel Mocellini as new head of customs control.

He added that he appointed public accountant Osmar Luis de Virgilio to administer the Buenos Aires customs offices and that all customs staff at Ezeiza International Airport outside the capital were "relieved" of their duties. It was unclear how many were fired.
Authorities recently revealed a "parallel" customs service was being run by crooked officials who smuggled $10 billion into the country, depriving the government of $3 billion in lost customs duties.
